text: What was the main objective of the Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation (LPG) policy initiated in 1991?
options: To reduce the role of the public sector in the economy
To increase the role of the public sector in the economy
To reduce tariffs and open up the economy to foreign investment
To increase tariffs and reduce foreign investment
correctAnswer: To reduce tariffs and open up the economy to foreign investment
explanation: The LPG policy aimed to reduce the role of the government in the economy, increase competition, and attract foreign investment. This was done by reducing tariffs, allowing foreign direct investment (FDI), and promoting globalisation.
subject: Economics

text: What is the role of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in India's economic reforms?
options: To impose tariffs and restrict trade
To reduce tariffs and promote free trade
To regulate foreign investment and disinvestment
To promote economic growth and development
correctAnswer: To reduce tariffs and promote free trade
explanation: The WTO is an international organisation that promotes free trade and reduces tariffs among its member countries. India's membership in the WTO has helped to reduce tariffs and promote trade, which has contributed to the country's economic growth.
subject: Economics

text: What is the impact of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) on the Indian economy?
options: It has led to a decline in economic growth
It has led to an increase in economic growth
It has had no impact on economic growth
It has led to a decline in employment
correctAnswer: It has led to an increase in economic growth
explanation: FDI has contributed to the growth of the Indian economy by bringing in new technologies, management practices, and capital. It has also led to the creation of new jobs and increased competition, which has benefited consumers.
subject: Economics

text: What is the significance of disinvestment in the Indian economy?
options: It has led to a decline in government revenue
It has led to an increase in government revenue
It has had no impact on government revenue
It has led to a decline in economic growth
correctAnswer: It has led to an increase in government revenue
explanation: Disinvestment refers to the sale of government-owned assets to private companies. This has helped to increase government revenue and reduce the burden on taxpayers. It has also promoted private sector participation in key sectors such as infrastructure and energy.
subject: Economics

text: What is the impact of tariffs on the Indian economy?
options: It has led to a decline in economic growth
It has led to an increase in economic growth
It has had no impact on economic growth
It has led to a decline in employment
correctAnswer: It has led to a decline in economic growth
explanation: Tariffs refer to taxes imposed on imported goods. High tariffs can lead to a decline in economic growth by reducing competition and increasing prices. However, low tariffs can promote trade and economic growth by increasing competition and reducing prices.
subject: Economics

text: What is the role of the government in promoting foreign direct investment (FDI) in India?
options: To impose restrictions on FDI
To promote FDI through incentives and policies
To have no role in promoting FDI
To reduce FDI
correctAnswer: To promote FDI through incentives and policies
explanation: The government has taken various measures to promote FDI in India, including offering incentives such as tax breaks, subsidies, and streamlined regulatory processes. This has helped to attract foreign investment and promote economic growth.
subject: Economics

text: What is the impact of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on India's trade policies?
options: It has led to a decline in trade
It has led to an increase in trade
It has had no impact on trade
It has led to a decline in economic growth
correctAnswer: It has led to an increase in trade
explanation: The WTO has promoted free trade and reduced tariffs among its member countries. This has helped to increase India's trade with other countries and promote economic growth.
subject: Economics

text: What is the significance of the 1991 economic reforms in India?
options: It has led to a decline in economic growth
It has led to an increase in economic growth
It has had no impact on economic growth
It has led to a decline in employment
correctAnswer: It has led to an increase in economic growth
explanation: The 1991 economic reforms were a major turning point in India's economic history. They helped to liberalise the economy, promote foreign investment, and increase economic growth. The reforms have also helped to reduce poverty and improve living standards.
subject: Economics
